ghost.name: Ghost
ghost.description: Place a second image over the piece with a screen blend: only its light values survive.

stain.name: Stain
stain.description: Place a second image over the piece with a multiply blend: only its dark values survive.

stamp.name: Stamp
stamp.description: Cut out an image and stamp it onto the canvas.

reverberate.name: Reverberate
reverberate.description: Cut out an image's subject and paint with it. Every stroke lays down repeated stamps along its path.

rails.name: Rails
rails.description: A random image is broken into fragments that arrive as a flat, single-color stencil. Arrange it, set the color, erase what you don't want.

char.name: Char
char.description: A random image is broken into fragments that keep the photo's own pixels. Arrange them, then darken and desaturate them toward black.

deeper.name: Deeper
deeper.description: Frame a region of the piece and crop to go deeper into the image. Upscaling restores the pixel values by 4x.

closer.name: Closer
closer.description: Frame a region of the piece and crop to get closer into the image. No upscaling, faithful to the pixels.

rack.name: Rack
rack.description: The whole piece comes loose as one object: drag, scale, rotate, flip it. Whatever leaves the canvas is cut off; whatever the move uncovers stays white.

lift.name: Lift
lift.description: Copy a rectangle of the piece and stamp it down elsewhere. The source stays where it is: a second impression, cropped where it runs off the edge.

fracture.name: Fracture
fracture.description: The whole piece breaks into chunks and slides apart. Seed the distribution, size the chunks, then erase the fracture back wherever the piece should stay whole.

dust.name: Dust
dust.description: Paint monochrome grain onto the piece. Nothing changes until you paint.

bruise.name: Bruise
bruise.description: Set the discoloration, then paint where the image should bruise.

blur.name: Blur
blur.description: Paint blur onto the piece with a brush. Nothing changes until you paint.

steep.name: Steep
steep.description: Flood the whole canvas with one color - pick the dye and the blend mode. Influence is steeping time.

hue.name: Hue
hue.description: Shift hue, saturation, and brightness across the whole canvas. Influence sets how strongly it applies.

cure.name: Cure
cure.description: The piece is blended over itself - contrast deepens, midtones richen. Influence is how far the cure has gone.

etch.name: Subliminal Etch
etch.description: Place a small frame, zoom to its pixels, and draw a glyph square by square. At full size it will be almost nothing.

searcher.name: Searcher
searcher.description: Look through everything left in the deck and take any card. The chosen card is the next action.

skim.name: Skim
skim.description: Turn the deck's top card face-up. Keep it on top for the next deal, or bury it back into the deck.

delay.name: Delay
delay.description: The first Coda dealt can be set aside, once. It shuffles back into the deck and can return on the very next draw.

transfer.name: Transfer
transfer.description: The whole piece is redrawn in a painted style. Erase to cut the original back through; Influence sets how strongly the redraw sits.

shatteredTransfer.name: Shattered Transfer
shatteredTransfer.description: The piece is redrawn in a painted style, but the redraw shows through only where a stencil sits. The stencil is cut from another image's fragments. Drag it, scale it, erase through it.

stashReturn.name: Stash Return
stashReturn.description: The image you stashed returns. Place it into the piece as it now stands.

coda.name: Coda
coda.description: The piece is finished. The session ends here.

ground.hint: The color under the image. It bakes in with the arrangement when you draw.

opening.title: THE OPENING
opening.hint: Take two: one to *place now*, one to *stash for later*. Or click the stashed one again to *place both*, holding nothing back.

deckOverlay.codaSomewhere: …and the Coda is somewhere in here.

guide.title: THE GUIDE
guide.close: Esc or the × closes. The page names above open the other areas.

folders.title: The folders
folders.p1: **Input** is read-only: the images sessions deal from. **Output** is where finished pieces land at full resolution. Both must exist before a session begins; paths take a leading `~` for home.
folders.p2: **Card faces** is optional: a folder of alternate face sets, one subfolder per set. The built-in faces stand whenever it is empty.

deck.title: The deck line
deck.p1: The deck named here is the one the next session shuffles. The **Deck editor** is where decks are assembled, saved, and chosen.

doors.title: The two ways in
doors.p1: **Begin session** opens the studio. **Foundry** opens the wing that casts card faces. Each returns here when its work is done, and everything on this screen is remembered per machine.

what.title: What this is
what.p1: Zyme is a studio for digital collage, worked one card at a time. Each round deals a single card from a deck, and the card decides the one thing you can do that round: a brush to paint with, a frame to move, a color to soak the canvas in. You work inside that constraint, then draw from the deck, which commits the round and turns the next card in one gesture.

arc.title: The arc of a session
arc.opening: **The opening**: take two images from the grid, one placed now, one stashed for later.
arc.placement: **Placement**: arrange the image. Drag to move, handles to scale and rotate, the mask brush to erase what shouldn't survive.
arc.actOne: **Act I**: a handful of rounds, one dealt card each.
arc.stash: **The stash returns**: its card is shuffled into the deck as soon as you stash, and the image you held back comes home when that card is drawn. That could be the very first round, much later, or never, if the Coda arrives first.
arc.actTwo: **Act II**: the Coda is shuffled into the deck. Deal by deal, it is coming.
arc.coda: **The Coda**: the piece is finished, and writes to your output folder at full resolution.

commitment.title: Commitment
commitment.p1: **The draw is permanent.** Every card you draw bakes the canvas down to one flat image; there is no undo across rounds and no stepping back. Undo lives only inside a round, for brush strokes.
commitment.p2: Closing the tab abandons the piece in progress. None of this is missing; commitment is the discipline the deck imposes.

brush.title: The brush
brush.p1: Whenever an image is loose on the canvas, the mask brush is at hand: **erase** paints an image away, **restore** brings it back, **soften** feathers an edge. A mask belongs to its image. It travels through every move, scale, and rotation.
brush.p2: Cmd/Ctrl+Z takes back a stroke, Shift added redoes it, within the round only. No undo crosses a draw.

deckCards.title: Cards that work the deck
deckCards.p1: Most cards work the piece; a few work the deck itself. **Skim** turns the top card, and you keep it or bury it. **Searcher** takes the card the piece needs. **Delay** grants a held right: the first Coda dealt can be set aside, once.
deckCards.p2: You always know *what* remains in the deck, never the order it arrives in. The Coda ends the session when it is accepted.

bearings.title: Finding your way
bearings.p1: The deck is the button: it waits at the foot of the panel, and one click on it commits the round and flips the next card face-up beside it. Enter does the same from the keyboard.
bearings.p2: Every control names its key when you hover it; the full map is behind **keys** in the header. **View the deck** shows what has been spent, in order, and what remains, in none.

what.title: What a deck is
what.p1: A deck is a recipe: which cards, and how many copies of each. A session shuffles that recipe and deals it. Change the recipe and you change the kind of piece a session produces.

rules.title: The rules of assembly
rules.p1: A deck holds **12 to 20 cards**. The cap is the point: a small deck is one you can hold in your head, so you always know roughly what's left. Copies of one card are capped too: weight a deck toward a card, don't fill it with one.
rules.p2: The Codas are never edited here. Three are always shuffled in late, whatever the deck holds. The ending is not optional.

saved.title: Saving and using
saved.p1: Name a deck to save it; saved decks live on this machine only. **Use this deck** hands it to the next session, and the house deck is always there to come back to.

what.title: What the foundry is
what.p1: The foundry is Zyme's second wing: sessions that cast the card faces themselves. A cast is one session for one face, worked under constraint and sealed for good, like any piece.

arc.title: The arc of a cast
arc.commission: **The commission**: the card this face is for. Choose it, or let the deck decide.
arc.plate: **The plate**: take one of the dealt blanks. Its frame is the card's fixed anatomy, and the white window waits for art. Taking the plate also fixes the run: how many impressions this cast will pull.
arc.panel: **The panel**: take an image and arrange it under the window; the plate's edge crops whatever crosses it.
arc.type: **The type**: name, type line, and description are set on the face. Double-click to edit, drag to nudge, re-deal the fonts until it reads right.
arc.press: **The Press**: the foundry's one irreversible commit. Art, plate, and type flatten to pixels for good; after it, a working deck deals cards that mark the sealed face.
arc.rounds: **The working rounds**: each dealt card marks the sealed face its own way. The deck is the button here too: it waits at the foot of the panel, and one click on it commits the round in hand and turns the next card face-up beside it. Enter does the same.
arc.proof: **The Proof**: the finished cast writes to your casts folder, with the full-resolution master alongside. A run returns to the sealed base for the next impression.

play.title: Putting a face in play
play.p1: A cast comes into play through a card-faces set: a folder of PNGs named by card id, one subfolder per set. Point Setup's *card faces* field at that folder and choose the set. Every deal after that wears your faces.

keys.title: KEYS
keys.close: Click anywhere or press Esc to close.

always.title: Always
always.Enter: The deck, from the keyboard: commit the round and turn the next card, or begin again. Never confirms the opening pick.
always.Cmd/Ctrl + drag: Pan: grab the canvas and move it, to work closer or farther.
always.Hold Space + drag: Pan, the same way. Whichever hold you reach for.
always.0: Reset the view, back to fit.
always.Shift+R: Restart. It destroys the piece, so it takes two keys.
always.Esc: Back out: deselect, put a grid pick back, discard a copy in hand, close this.

brush.title: Brush in hand
brush.[ ]: Brush size, steps of 5 (10 with Shift). Shift+drag on the canvas also resizes.
brush.W: Arrange, where there is something to arrange.
brush.Cmd/Ctrl+Z: Undo a stroke; add Shift to redo. Never crosses a draw.

certainCards.title: On certain cards
certainCards.Enter: Confirm a grid pick. Etch: zoom in.
certainCards.N: A new hue on any color control.
